title: The Drug Payment Stages of a Ridgecrest RxSecure Plan Year
content:
A member of a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan moves through the payment stages in one direction over the contract year, and the stage they are in decides what they pay at the counter.

**The deductible stage.** The member pays the negotiated price of every fill whose formulary tier the deductible applies to, until what they have paid reaches the annual deductible of the plan held.

**The initial coverage stage.** The member pays the cost share their plan and pharmacy give, and every dollar they pay counts toward the annual out-of-pocket threshold.

**Catastrophic coverage.** It begins on the fill that takes the member's true out-of-pocket total to the annual out-of-pocket threshold, and from that fill on the member pays nothing for covered drugs for the rest of the contract year.

## How the stages move

- A fill that straddles a stage boundary is split at the boundary, so the member pays the earlier stage's cost share only up to the distance remaining and the later stage's terms on the rest.
- Reversing a fill takes its member payment back out of the accumulator and can return the member to an earlier stage; the stages are restated from the accumulator rather than kept as a separate fact.
- The stages reset to the deductible stage on 1 January, whatever the member reached the year before.
- A member who asks why their total has not moved is shown which of their payments counted and which did not.

## A clause no longer in force

The following clause of this policy is **no longer in force** and is set out here only so that it is not applied: "Only what the member or a qualifying third party actually paid counts toward the threshold: plan payments, premiums and the late enrollment penalty never count" — no longer in force.
